rules.short: Open on one trend people really do, shown being done
Give the real dates and times, not just 'coming soon'
A product carousel shows Aneet holding the tube, after the facts

sun.name: A brand playing office, its skin officer stopping people mid-trend
sun.line: A beauty brand posting two or three times a day, on a running story fronted by Aneet's officer. [Aneet stopping a girl's ice facial](P07) holds 30% of the likes of all 30 posts.

doss.going: Lakmē is a make-up and skincare brand posting two or three times a day. In these 30 posts it is making one person the face of its feed: Aneet Padda, playing a made-up Skin Goals Officer in a vest and tie. Every skincare product gets sold through her, in a short comedy where she stops someone mid-trend or in a carousel where she holds the tube. It keeps its Fashion Week dates up and fills the gaps with makeup shots and zodiac boards. It is for young women who follow beauty trends.
doss.landing: Followers reward Aneet rescuing someone. Her ten pink-studio reels hold 87% of the likes, typically 7.1× its usual. The longest episodes went furthest, [the chilli reel](P21) at 74× and [the layering episode](P26) at 65×. Posts without her sit near the usual: [the Ganpati checklist](P13) at 41% and [the blush swatches](P22) at 62%. Real dates carry too, as [the Fashion Week schedule](P29) went 7.4×. The last ten posts ran 2.2× the usual with eight of them above it, against three of ten in mid-September. Time of day and weekday show nothing beyond chance.
doss.take: Put a person in the middle of a trend viewers really do, then let one character step in and fix it. Give real dates rather than 'coming soon'. Hold the product in a hand, and keep grids and bare checklists to filler.

planets.name: Product posts
planets.what: Posts that show a product: gel, serum, balm, cream, swatches, a packed phone case, a mock tweet.

doss.going: To keep the range in front of people between the episodes.
doss.landing: A product post needs a person or a use in it. Five of the seven beat its usual, but together they hold only 4% of the likes. [The Peach Milk gel carousel](P09) went 3.4× and [the serum carousel](P16) 2.2×, both with Aneet in them. With nobody in them, [the blush swatches](P22) got 62% and [the car-seat tweet](P28) 70%. The same gel drew far less here than in the ice episode: 3.4× against 92×.
doss.take: Put a person or a use in the product post. A swatch or a jar on its own sits near or under the usual.

each.8: The gel scooped like sorbet, with Aneet tapping her cheek. It went 3.4×.
each.15: Serum and crème, with Aneet dabbing cream on slide three. It went 2.2×.
each.18: Five minis packed into a phone case. It went 1.9×.
each.21: Seven blush shades swiped down an arm, one prompt repeated. It got 62% of its usual.
each.22: Balm swatches, with Aneet arriving on slide four. It went 1.9×.
each.26: CC cream facts first, Aneet catching the tube on slide three. It went 2.0×.
each.27: Five products buckled into a car seat as a joke. It got 70% of its usual.

planets.name: Officer's calls
planets.what: Short reels where Aneet, in vest and tie, talks to the camera as the Skin Goals Officer and ends on the desk card.

doss.going: To make the officer a face people know before the series arrives, one habit at a time.
doss.landing: The short monologues are the reliable base: all six beat its usual. [Aneet's 13-second ice-dunking warning](P04) is the best of them at 11×, because it names one habit and gets out. [The three-rules reel](P01) did 7.3×. [The Monday calendar reel](P24) names a feeling instead of a habit and did 2.6×. They are cooling, from 7.3× early to 4.7× lately.
doss.take: Name one plain habit in the first two seconds. A feeling or a list gives less.

each.0: Three rules to copy, then four products pop up. It went 7.3×.
each.2: It opens on a phone map for four seconds before she speaks. It went 3.5×.
each.3: Ice dunking named at once, over in 13 seconds. It went 11×.
each.10: Six actives counted on her fingers, on screen from 0:00. It went 4.7×.
each.17: Chilli lip oil called out, with a namaste and a sign-off. It went 6.8×.
each.23: A Monday calendar for a chaotic routine, under the paid label. It went 2.6×.

planets.name: List carousels
planets.what: Carousels and graphics built on a list: zodiac boards, love languages, beauty rules, a checklist.

doss.going: Lists give a reader something to find themself in, with a product on the way.
doss.landing: Lists get a lukewarm response. Four of the six beat its usual, but the typical one sits level with it, well under the 1.9× of the product posts. [The love languages of a makeup girl](P10) did best at 1.6×. [The Ganpati checklist](P13), where nothing moves and nobody speaks, did worst at 41%. A second telling of the zodiac boards fell to 71%.
doss.take: A list works as a title. Skip a part two of anything only average, and put a person in.

each.5: Six star signs, each paired with a lip shade. It held about its usual.
each.9: Each slide is one line a reader sees themself in. It went 1.6×.
each.11: Warnings first, then the full look on slide six. It held about its usual.
each.12: Nine boxes to tick, closing Ganpati season. It got 41% of its usual.
each.13: The same boards for six more signs. It got 71% of its usual.
each.16: Four myths with a pinned product under each. It held about its usual.

planets.name: Skinterventions episodes
planets.what: Sketches where someone does a trend, Aneet steps in, and the pink briefcase opens on the fix.

doss.going: They turn a product pitch into a short comedy: the trend, the rescue, the product.
doss.landing: These four are the account. All four beat its usual, and together they hold 76% of the likes. Three of them went 65 to 92×. [Aneet stopping a girl's ice facial](P07), [the chilli reel](P21) and [the layering episode](P26) each open on something viewers have seen or done. [Episode 2](P15) opens on a live stream reading out acid names, with nothing to picture, and got 1.9×. They are holding up well.
doss.take: Open on a habit people recognise, shown being done, before the rescue. Episode 2 shows the opening matters more than the product.

each.6: A girl dunks her face in ice and Aneet steps in with the gel. It went 92×.
each.14: Acid names read out on a live stream first. It went 1.9×.
each.20: A woman reaches for chilli at 0:03 and Aneet answers with the balm. It went 74×.
each.25: A friend layers six products before a meeting and Aneet opens the briefcase. It went 65×.

planets.name: Fashion Week posts
planets.what: Posts for Lakmē Fashion Week x FDCI in New Delhi: a dates poster, a finale montage co-posted with FDCI, and the full schedule.

doss.going: The account wants to be where people check the dates for its own runway week.
doss.landing: Dates are the draw. All three beat its usual, and [the Fashion Week schedule carousel](P29), which lists every show day by day, went 7.4×. [The dates poster](P05) puts the dates and New Delhi on one image and did 4.7×. [The finale montage](P25) is the co-post with FDCI under the paid label and shows one date between runway clips, so it stayed at 1.3×. The fuller the dates, the further it went.
doss.take: Post the full schedule, not a teaser with one date tucked inside.

each.4: Three models in knitwear, dates and city readable at once. It went 4.7×.
each.24: Archive runway looks, with one date on screen for four seconds. It went 1.3×.
each.28: Seven slides, every show and time. It went 7.4×.

planets.name: Kareena posts
planets.what: Two posts for brand ambassador Kareena Kapoor Khan: her birthday and a kajal award.

doss.going: A clear occasion to post: a birthday and an award.
doss.landing: She works when there is a reason to post. Both beat its usual: [the Kareena birthday montage](P02) went 3.2× and [the kajal award](P08) 2.0×. Both lean on things viewers already know her for, famous film lines and characters, and comments ran 74% of the usual for the likes. Two posts are too few to call a trend.
doss.take: Use her for a clear occasion. The occasion carries it; her face alone would not.

each.1: Film roles and a famous line for her birthday. It went 3.2×.
each.7: The kajal wins an award, explained over four slides. It went 2.0×.

planets.name: One-offs
planets.what: Posts that aren't a kind yet: a pop-up recap and a festive teaser.

doss.going: Two event moments: a pop-up café and the lead-up to a festive launch.
doss.landing: Neither is a pattern yet. [The festive glam mood-board collage](P30) teased a launch with no date and went 2.5×; [the pop-up recap](P20) went 1.4×. Both beat its usual, and a dated launch post would be the real test.
doss.take: Wait before naming a kind. A dated launch post would be the test of the teaser.

each.19: Guests colour cups and get caricatures. It went 1.4×.
each.29: Disco glitter and sweets, 'loading'. It went 2.5×.

planets.name: Zodiac lip shades
planets.what: A two-part series pairing star signs with 9to5 lip shades and mood boards.

doss.going: To show the lip range through something readers find themselves in.
doss.landing: The zodiac boards show a series fading. [Part one](P06) held about its usual. [Part two](P14), the same boards again with nothing new to wait for, fell to 71%. Zodiac drew comments, 1.6× the usual for its likes, but few likes.
doss.take: Skip a part two of anything that was only average.

each.5: Part one, six signs. It held about its usual.
each.13: Part two, six more signs. It got 71% of its usual.

planets.name: Festive season
planets.what: The festive run-up: a Ganpati sign-off checklist and a Festive Glam teaser.

doss.going: To mark the season and tease a launch.
doss.landing: A season is a reason to post, and it only helps if something moves. [The festive glam mood-board collage](P30) teased a launch with a collage and went 2.5×. [The Ganpati checklist](P13), nine boxes to tick, got 41%, the lowest of all 30 posts.
doss.take: A season is a reason to post, but a checklist where nothing moves is not a post people stop on.

each.12: Nine ticks to close Ganpati season. It got 41% of its usual.
each.29: Festive Glam Loading, no date. It went 2.5×.

planets.name: Aneet Padda
planets.what: Aneet Padda, playing Lakmē's Skin Goals Officer in a white sleeveless vest and necktie, often with a pink-stickered briefcase and an ID badge.

doss.going: One face people recognise from post to post, so every pitch has the same character behind it.
doss.landing: Aneet is the account. She is in 14 posts, every one beat Lakmē's usual, and together they took 90% of the likes. How far she goes depends on the job. Let her interrupt a stranger mid-trend, as in [the ice facial](P07) and [the chilli reel](P21), and she goes 92× and 74×. Put her on the last slide of a carousel and she adds about double: [the balm carousel](P23) did 1.9×. The vest and tie are constant, so they explain little; [the Monday calendar reel](P24) wore them and did 2.6×. She is cooling a little: her last seven ran 2.6×, down from 4.7×.
doss.take: She works in every format, but the sketches are where she is huge. In a carousel expect about double the usual, not 70 times.

each.0: Three rules in a tie. It went 7.3×.
each.2: She reads a map of skin emergencies. It went 3.5×.
each.3: Ice dunking in 13 seconds. It went 11×.
each.6: She stops an ice facial. It went 92×.
each.8: She taps her cheek over the gel. It went 3.4×.

each.22: She blows on her glossy lips on slide four. It went 1.9×.
each.25: She rescues a friend layering six products. It went 65×.
each.26: She catches the tube on slide three. It went 2.0×.

planets.name: Hya Beach Edit
planets.what: The Hya Beach Edit makeup line: blush stick, liner and lipstick duo, concealer, setting spray, lip gloss.

doss.going: It gives the account makeup to sell beyond skincare.
doss.landing: Hya Beach Edit never got a sketch, and it shows. Half of the six beat its usual and the typical post sits level with it. [The phone-case reel](P19) did best at 1.9× because it shows a use. [The myths carousel](P17) and [the office-makeup warnings](P12) argue with beauty rules and held about the same. Products with no idea behind them sagged: [the Ganpati checklist](P13) got 41% and [the blush swatches](P22) 62%. [The car-seat tweet](P28) got 70%. The line is wearing out, too.
doss.take: Give the products an argument or a use, a myth or an office rule, rather than a swatch with nothing else.

each.11: Trends not to wear to work, then all of them. It held about its usual.
each.12: Hya setting spray and duo on a checklist. It got 41% of its usual.
each.16: Hya cushion, concealer and blush under four myths. It held about its usual.
each.18: Hya minis in a phone case. It went 1.9×.
each.21: Seven Hya blush shades. It got 62% of its usual.
each.27: Hya blush, duo and mist in a car seat. It got 70% of its usual.

planets.name: 9to5 lips and crayons
planets.what: Lakmē 9to5 lipsticks, glosses and crayons: the zodiac boards, love languages and the Crayon Café pop-up.

doss.going: To keep the 9to5 lip range in front of people through lists and an event.
doss.landing: The lip range sells as a theme with no story behind it. Three of the four beat its usual, typically 1.2×. [The love languages carousel](P10) did best at 1.6× and [the pop-up recap](P20) went 1.4×. [Zodiac part one](P06) held about the same and [part two](P14) fell to 71%. None of the four has a sketch in it.
doss.take: Lips sell best through a sketch like the chilli episode. A themed catalogue only holds the usual.

each.5: Six signs with lip shades. It held about its usual.
each.9: Lipstick and gloss among five love languages. It went 1.6×.
each.13: Lip stain, gloss and oil, six signs. It got 71% of its usual.
each.19: Lip crayons at a pop-up. It went 1.4×.

planets.name: Peptide Lip I.V.
planets.what: The Peptide Lip I.V. balm, sold in the chilli episode and a carousel.

doss.going: Sold as the painless alternative to rubbing chilli on your lips.
doss.landing: The balm shows what an episode does for a product. [Aneet stopping a woman rubbing chilli on her lips](P21) sold it at 74×, while [the balm carousel](P23), a list of ingredients with Aneet on the last slide, got 1.9×. Both beat its usual, though comments ran only 32% of the usual for the likes.
doss.take: Sell the balm as the fix to something viewers have really tried, not as an ingredient list.

each.20: Four balm tubes in the briefcase, the fix for chilli. It went 74×.

planets.name: Perfect Radiance serum and crème
planets.what: Lakmē Perfect Radiance serum and day gel crème, pitched for pigmentation.

doss.going: Positioned as the officer's pick for pigmentation, pitched at the end of episode 2 and again in a carousel.
doss.landing: The serum never got a trend to answer. Both posts beat its usual, but neither comes near the ice or chilli episodes. [Episode 2](P15) opens on a live stream with nothing to picture and went 1.9×. [The serum carousel](P16) went 2.2×, helped by Aneet dabbing the cream on slide three.
doss.take: The pitch is fine but the set-up was weak. Pair this serum with a trend people really do.

each.14: Serum handed to a woman after the acid talk. It went 1.9×.
each.15: Serum, crème and textures, with Aneet applying. It went 2.2×.

planets.name: 9to5 CC Cream
planets.what: Lakmē 9to5 CC+ cream, sold as skincare and makeup in one step.

doss.going: It is aimed at someone rushing before a meeting.
doss.landing: The cream sells best as the way out of a morning rush. [Aneet rescuing a friend who layers six products](P26) went 65× because most viewers have done that rush. [The CC cream carousel](P27), facts first with Aneet catching the tube on slide three, went 2.0×. Both beat its usual.
doss.take: Show the morning problem the cream solves. Facts alone give a decent carousel but not a big one.

each.25: The cream is the fix for six layered products. It went 65×.
each.26: Tube, callouts, Aneet and a creator applying. It went 2.0×.

planets.name: Peach Milk Icy Sorbet Gel
planets.what: The Peach Milk Icy Sorbet Gel, the cooling answer to ice facials.

doss.going: It is sold first in the ice episode and then in a carousel.
doss.landing: The gel is one big post and one ordinary one. [Aneet stopping a girl's ice facial](P07) did 92× and holds 31% of the likes; [the gel carousel](P09) did 3.4×. The episode is a sketch where the gel answers a problem viewers recognise. The carousel shows a scoop and an ingredient list. Both beat its usual.
doss.take: A product lands harder as the answer to a problem someone just did on screen than as a jar on its own.

each.6: The gel in the briefcase after the ice dunk. It went 92×.
each.8: The jar on slide one, scooped like sorbet. It went 3.4×.

planets.name: Eyeconic Kajal
planets.what: The turquoise Eyeconic Kajal, shown with its award and in a love-language joke.

doss.going: To get the kajal seen through a face and a joke.
doss.landing: The kajal needs a face or a joke. [Kareena announcing the kajal award](P08) has Kareena holding it, with the award explained over four slides, and went 2.0×. [The love languages carousel](P10) puts it among lipsticks and glosses and did 1.6×. Both beat its usual, and neither is a sketch.
doss.take: A person or a joke gets the kajal seen.

each.7: Kareena announces the Best Eye Pencil award. It went 2.0×.
each.9: Kajal as one of five love languages. It went 1.6×.

planets.name: Paid-label posts
planets.what: The three posts with a paid label: the Monday-calendar reel, the Fashion Week finale montage and the CC cream episode.

doss.going: Two carry a co-author: Aneet's own account on the CC cream episode, FDCI and another account on the finale.
doss.landing: The paid label predicts nothing. All three beat its usual and together hold 23% of the likes. [Aneet rescuing a friend who layers six products](P26) went 65× because it is an episode. [The Monday calendar reel](P24) did 2.6× as a feeling and [the finale montage](P25) 1.3× as a montage.
doss.take: The paid label does not change what works. Put it on an episode, not a montage.

each.23: Paid label on a monologue. It went 2.6×.
each.24: Co-authored with FDCI and another account. It went 1.3×.
each.25: Co-authored with Aneet's account. It went 65×.

planets.name: Pink studio
planets.what: The pink studio set: pastel backdrop, a desk with an ID badge, the pink briefcase, and the Skinterventions title card.

doss.going: A set that looks the same every time tells the viewer which show this is.
doss.landing: The pink studio is where the officer lives, and it doesn't pick winners. It is the same ten posts as her reels, all above its usual, and together they hold 87% of the likes. What changes the result is the trend in front of the wall. [Aneet stopping a girl's ice facial](P07) went 92× and [the layering episode](P26) 65×. [Episode 2](P15) opens on a live stream inside the same set and got 1.9×.
doss.take: Keep the set, change the trend. The same pink wall holds both 92× and 1.9×.

laws.law: Open on one trend people really do, shown being done.
laws.short: Open on one trend people really do, shown being done

sides.lands: A trend someone is seen doing
sides.sinks: A list, or a feeling about routines

stat.u: the two episodes that play a trend out

laws.why: [A woman reaches for chilli to plump her lips](P21) at 0:03, and [a friend layers six products for a no-makeup look](P26) from 0:03; each is something a viewer has seen or done, and Aneet steps in at 0:14 and 0:17. [Episode 2](P15) opened on a live stream reading out acid names, so there was nothing to picture. [Aneet comparing a routine to a Monday calendar](P24) names a feeling, not a habit, and stayed at 2.6×. Both big reels were liked, not argued over: 8 and 14 comments per 1,000 likes, against a usual 43.
laws.take: Open the next episode on someone doing a trend most viewers have tried, and keep acid lists for carousels.

laws.why: [The Fashion Week schedule carousel](P29) lists every show for 13 to 18 October, day by day: something to screenshot and plan around, and the best carousel in 90 days. [The runway montage](P25) puts one date on screen from 0:07 to 0:11, between clips and partner logos, and stayed at 1.3×. [The poster](P05) with dates went 4.7×. [Aneet's Monday-calendar reel](P24) and [the festive 'loading' collage](P30) say soon with no date and landed at 2.6× and 2.5×.

laws.why: [The lip balm carousel](P23) ends on Aneet blowing on her lips with the tube up; [the CC cream carousel](P27) gives the facts on slides 1 and 2, then Aneet catching the tube on slide 3. Both came in near twice the usual carousel, like [the gel](P09) and [the serum](P16). [The pop-up recap](P20), [the myths](P17), [the zodiac boards](P14) and [the office-makeup collage](P12) show products with no one holding them. Aneet in a carousel adds about 2×; the 65 to 74 times belongs to the [episodes](L1).
